description: A polyphonic ADSR envelope with a stereo VCA built in. It chains automatically to a TZOP operator placed beside it, so an envelope can be added to a DX7 style algorithm without patching

params.text: Sets the time the envelope takes to rise to full
Sets the time the envelope takes to fall from full to the sustain level
Sets the level the envelope holds while the gate stays high
Sets the time the envelope takes to fall to zero once the gate drops
Bends the envelope segments between linear and exponential
Scales the height of the envelope; a negative setting inverts the shape
How much of the attack input reaches the attack time
How much of the decay input reaches the decay time
How much of the sustain input reaches the sustain level
How much of the release input reaches the release time
How much of the scale input reaches the scaling
A tap fires the envelope by hand
Switches the envelope from four stages to an attack and a release only
Starts the envelope again each time it finishes, so it runs as a repeating shape

inputs.text: A voltage modulating the attack time
A voltage modulating the decay time
A voltage modulating the sustain level
A voltage modulating the release time
A gate or trigger starts the envelope; the number of channels arriving here sets how many voices the module runs
One side of a stereo signal for the VCA built into the module, whose level the envelope controls

outputs.text: The envelope voltage, one polyphonic channel per voice
One side of the stereo signal after the envelope has set its level
The envelope voltage with its sign flipped

notes: a TZOP placed immediately to the left is read without patching, so an envelope can be added to a DX7 style algorithm by placing the two side by side
menu: Time Ranges — a submenu of Time Range: 1 second, Time Range: 10 second and Time Range: 100 second, setting the full span of the attack, decay and release knobs
